epics.title: Evaluation Foundations

items.title: Create evaluation definitions, events and jobs tables
items.description: Add a migration and ORM schema for three tables. Definitions hold process, stage, evaluator and benchmark keys, version, rubric JSON, Promptfoo suite reference, judge output schema and an active flag. Events hold one immutable row per human submission with project id, definition version references, subject type and id, reviewer user id, reviewer role key and label, indexed lineage columns, stage key, phase index, artifact content hash, criteria scores, outcome, reason codes, comment and an optional corrected artifact Blob reference. Jobs hold one row per event and evaluator, unique on that pair, with V2 run id, status, specification hash, summary and result Blob references. Do not add columns to PRDs or Interviews.
definitionOfDone: Migration creates the three tables with the unique event and evaluator constraint on jobs
ORM schema matches the migration
PRDs and Interviews tables are unchanged
Migration applies and rolls back cleanly in a test database
technicalDependencies: Drizzle ORM schema update after migration
nonFunctionalRequirements: Indexes support lookup by project, subject type, subject id and artifact hash
Events table exposes no update or delete path in the data access layer

items.title: Seed platform evaluation definitions
items.description: Seed active definitions under the orchestrated workflow process for the PRD human review stage and the three Interview phase stages. Each definition holds the five shared criteria keys with per-stage labels and help text, the 1–5 scale labels, reason codes (missing requirement, invented requirement, incorrect interpretation, too vague, wrong scope, acceptance criteria not testable, PRD and backlog inconsistency), the four outcomes, the allowed reviewer roles (product owner, BA, manager, developer, QA, other), the minimum low-score comment length, a minimal structural Promptfoo suite reference, and the judge output schema.
definitionOfDone: Four active definitions exist after migration: PRD human review and Interview phases 1 to 3
All definitions share the same five criteria keys and the same reason code and outcome sets
Each definition carries a Promptfoo suite reference and a judge output schema
Re-running the seed does not create duplicate rows
technicalDependencies: Events and definitions tables from the data model work
Existing seed or migration pattern for platform defaults
nonFunctionalRequirements: Seeds are idempotent and versioned so a later rubric change adds a new version instead of editing history

items.title: Define shared evaluation types
items.description: Add shared client and server types for the evaluation outcome, reason code, criteria scores, definition, human evaluation event, create request, job status, and the structured judge output (missed requirements, invented requirements, optional alignment score, recommended improvements, confidence).
definitionOfDone: Types compile in both client and server builds
Create request type excludes lineage and artifact hash fields
Judge output type matches the seeded judge schema
Router and UI import these types instead of redefining them
technicalDependencies: Shared types directory used by both client and server
nonFunctionalRequirements: Types are the single contract for the router, service and UI so field names cannot drift

features.title: Evaluation Data Model and Contracts
outOfScope: Denormalized latest-review columns on PRDs or Interviews
features.description: Gives Product-Owner, BA, Manager and Developer users a stable store for feedback, and gives Project Admin and Platform Admin users stable records to review, by defining the evaluation tables, seeded definitions and shared types.
dependencies: Existing PostgreSQL migration and Drizzle schema conventions

items.title: Add workflow-evaluation view and submit permissions
items.description: Follow the Add a Permission workflow to create the view and submit permission keys: migration, permission catalog entry, route middleware constants, admin role UI listing, and default grants for the roles used by Product-Owner, BA, Manager and Developer groups. Project Admin access to the outcomes screen reuses existing Admin access and adds no key.
definitionOfDone: Both permission keys exist in the database and the documented catalog
Admin roles screen can grant and revoke both keys
Default grants are applied and listed in the catalog
Tests cover allowed and denied access for each key
technicalDependencies: Permission catalog documented in the RBAC governance rule
nonFunctionalRequirements: Permission checks run on the server for every evaluation route

items.title: Gate evaluation routes and UI on the workflow-human-evaluation flag
items.description: Register the workflow-human-evaluation flag with targeting for the Apex project and named pilot projects. Add a server check that refuses evaluation requests, job starts and notifications when the flag is off for the project, and a client check that hides every feedback surface, the Workflow evaluations page and the hub when it is off.
definitionOfDone: Flag exists and targets the Apex project by default
Server returns a refusal for evaluation routes when the flag is off
Client renders no evaluation UI when the flag is off
Turning the flag off leaves Interview and PRD flows working
technicalDependencies: Feature flag service and useFeatureFlag hook
nonFunctionalRequirements: Flag evaluation uses the project from the session, not from the request body

features.title: Evaluation Permissions and Rollout Gate
features.description: Lets Platform Admin users roll the feature out by project, and lets Product-Owner, BA, Manager and Developer users read and submit feedback only when they hold the new permissions.
dependencies: RBAC governance rule and rbac-management workflow
Existing feature flag service and client hook

personaBehaviors.behavior: Roll out evaluation feature by project and manage permissions
Read and submit feedback only when they hold the new permissions

items.title: Resolve lineage and artifact content hashes
items.description: Add thin hooks on the Interview and PRD services that return skill path, skill version, model, ids, the phase count and current phase, and the artifact content for hashing. Build the artifact binding resolver: for a PRD, hash the PRD markdown plus canonical backlog JSON; for an Interview phase, hash the phase transcript slice plus linked context. Canonical form must ignore key order. Store a generation counter only where Apex already has one.
definitionOfDone: Same artifact input always yields the same hash
A change to PRD markdown, backlog content or phase context changes the hash
Backlog JSON key order does not change the hash
Document approval and owner approval services are unchanged
technicalDependencies: AI usage tracking and PRD thread kickoff data for skill and model
nonFunctionalRequirements: Hash computation completes well inside the 2 second submit budget
Hooks add no approval or phase gate

items.title: Build the workflow evaluation service
items.description: Build the deep service that validates a submission against its definition (five scores from 1 to 5, valid outcome, reason codes and minimum comment length when any score is 2 or lower, corrected artifact required for PRD accept after edits), derives reviewer role from project groups with a definition picklist when ambiguous, attaches server-resolved lineage and artifact hash, writes large corrected artifacts to Blob, and inserts the event append-only. Also list events by subject, newest first, capped near 50, defaulting to the current artifact hash.
definitionOfDone: Invalid scores, missing reasons, short comments and a missing corrected artifact are rejected with clear errors
A valid submission stores one event and no operation modifies it afterwards
Reviewer role is read-only when one group matches and a definition role is required otherwise
Unit tests cover each validation rule, role derivation, and project isolation
nonFunctionalRequirements: Submit returns within 2 seconds
Every read and write is scoped by project id

items.title: Add the workflow evaluations router
items.description: Mount a dedicated workflow evaluations router that reads definitions, lists events filtered by project, subject type, subject id and artifact version, creates an event, and reads one event with job status. Apply the view and submit permissions, the feature flag check and project scoping from the session. Keep the router generic over process, stage and subject so later processes reuse it.
definitionOfDone: Definitions, list, create and single-event routes respond per the shared types
Missing permission or an off flag returns a refusal
List supports the older-versions flag and the 50-event cap
Router tests cover permission, flag and cross-project access
technicalDependencies: Express router mounting and auth middleware
nonFunctionalRequirements: Client-supplied lineage and hash fields are ignored or rejected
Responses never include events from another project

features.title: Evaluation Service and API
features.description: Gives Product-Owner, BA, Manager and Developer users a reliable way to submit and read feedback, and gives Project Admin and Platform Admin users trustworthy records, through one evaluation service and one dedicated router.
dependencies: Interview and PRD services for lineage inputs

outOfScope: New columns on PRDs or Interviews
assumptions: Seeded definitions cover the PRD stage and three Interview phase stages
Registry keys follow the accepted Measured Improvement Loop ADR
epics.description: Apex stores no structured human judgment of AI-generated Interview context or PRDs, and no evaluation tables, permissions or services exist. This epic builds the data model, seeded definitions, permissions, rollout flag, and the service and router that every other part uses. It is the base of the evaluation plane in the Measured Improvement Loop ADR.
successMetrics: A valid submission returns within 2 seconds and stores one immutable event with server-resolved lineage and artifact hash

epics.title: Reviewer Feedback Capture

items.title: Build the definition-driven feedback form
items.description: Build a form that takes stage key, subject type and subject id, loads its labels, scale, reason codes, outcomes and role list from the definition, and shows the five 1–5 criteria, the outcome picker, and reason codes plus a required comment when any score is 2 or lower. It shows the derived reviewer role read-only or a picklist when ambiguous, and an optional corrected artifact input. It submits through the create mutation and refreshes history.
definitionOfDone: Form renders criteria, reasons and roles from definition data with no hard-coded copy
Low-score reasons and comment rules match the server rules
Submit errors from the server appear next to the relevant field
Component tests cover conditional fields and submit states
nonFunctionalRequirements: Form is keyboard-operable with labeled controls and visible validation messages
Uses theme tokens and CSS Modules

items.title: Build the feedback history list and query hooks
items.description: Build a read-only history list showing events newest first with scores, outcome, reason codes, reviewer role and date. It defaults to events matching the live artifact hash, highlights the latest event for that hash, and offers a control to show events for older versions. Add hooks for definitions, events by subject and submit, with list invalidation on submit.
definitionOfDone: History defaults to the current artifact version and can show older versions
Latest event for the current hash is visibly marked
Submitting a new event refreshes the list without a page reload
Component tests cover empty, populated and older-version states
nonFunctionalRequirements: List shows at most about 50 events and renders within 1 second for that size

items.title: Build the optional prompt controller
items.description: Build the controller that shows a dismissible modal the first time a subject and stage has no event, then leaves a persistent Quality feedback tab or panel and a light banner until someone submits or the user dismisses the banner for the session. Copy states that feedback is optional and improves the AI over time. Remember skips per user in the browser.
definitionOfDone: Modal appears once for a subject and stage with no event
Skip closes the modal and leaves the panel and banner
Submitting or dismissing removes the banner as specified
Component tests cover first view, skip, submit and repeat visit
nonFunctionalRequirements: Modal traps and restores focus and closes with the Escape key
No prompt state ever disables a workflow action

Submit control appears only with the submit permission
Approve and Request Revision behave exactly as before
Component tests cover tab visibility by flag and permission
nonFunctionalRequirements: Tab loads lazily and adds no delay to opening the PRD

userStory.soThat: Apex learns how well its PRD generation met the need

BR-006: Lineage is resolved by the server

nonFunctionalRequirements.performance: Reason fields appear immediately when a score changes to 2 or lower
nonFunctionalRequirements.accessibility: Reason code list and comment field are labeled and errors are announced to screen readers

items.title: Skip the PRD feedback prompt

BR-016: The modal appears once per subject and stage with no event

Prompt fires once per phase stage when that phase ends

epics.title: Automated Diagnostic Jobs

items.title: Build the diagnostic execution specification
items.description: Build, on App Service, the immutable execution specification for each job type. It carries the redacted artifact package (excerpt, backlog slice, transcript context), rubric version, suite reference, artifact hash, human scores as reference hints, and the resolved judge model (project evaluation model when set, otherwise the PRD validation default). Every value the worker needs is a required field checked by the specification's type guard, and the worker supplies no defaults.
definitionOfDone: Specification carries the same artifact hash as the human event
Judge model resolves from project setting, then default, on App Service
A missing required field makes the type guard reject the specification
Unit tests cover both job types and the fallback model
technicalDependencies: V2 execution specification types and type guards
Project settings and PRD validation model resolution
nonFunctionalRequirements: A specification missing a required value is refused before any model call
Specification contents are limited to what the judge needs

items.title: Create and enqueue two jobs on every submission
items.description: After a human event is stored, create one Promptfoo job and one LLM judge job, unique per event and evaluator, and enqueue each as a V2 run using the existing admission pattern. If enqueue fails, keep the event and mark that job failed. Do not enqueue on reads. A resubmission creates a new event and a new pair of jobs.
definitionOfDone: Each stored event has exactly two job rows with distinct evaluator keys
Enqueue failure marks the job failed and leaves the event stored
Reading an event or list creates no jobs
Tests cover resubmission and the unique event and evaluator rule
nonFunctionalRequirements: Enqueue happens outside the 2 second submit response path
Submit succeeds even when enqueue fails

items.title: Add manual retry for failed jobs
items.description: Add a router operation that re-enqueues a failed job for an event after checking that the caller can open Project Admin for the project or is a Platform Admin. Rebuild the specification from the stored event so the artifact hash is unchanged. Reject retries of jobs that are not failed.
definitionOfDone: A failed job can be retried and returns to pending
Pending, running and ready jobs cannot be retried
Callers without admin access are refused
Tests cover success, wrong state and denied access
nonFunctionalRequirements: Retry returns promptly with the new job status
Retry is scoped to the caller's project

items.title: Log usage and cost for diagnostic runs
items.description: Record token usage and cost for both job types through AI usage tracking, tagged with the event id and the evaluation feature so AI cost analytics can attribute spend.
definitionOfDone: Each completed job writes a usage record tied to its event id
Usage appears under a distinct evaluation feature label in cost analytics
Tests cover the logging call and logging failure handling
nonFunctionalRequirements: Usage logging failure does not fail the job

features.title: Diagnostic Job Orchestration
features.description: Gives Project Admin and Platform Admin users diagnostics for every human event by creating, enqueuing, tracking and retrying two background jobs per submission.
dependencies: Existing V2 admission and execution specification pattern

items.title: Run the Promptfoo suite on the V2 worker
items.description: Add a worker executor that runs the Promptfoo suite named on the execution specification against the artifact package, returns a summary, and writes full output to Blob. The executor holds no database connection and no defaults.
definitionOfDone: A valid specification produces a summary and a Blob output reference
A specification missing a required value is refused
The no-database-import test passes
Tests cover pass, suite failure and refused specification
technicalDependencies: Promptfoo runtime in the worker image
nonFunctionalRequirements: Worker import graph contains no database module
A suite failure is reported as a failed job, not a crash

items.title: Run the LLM judge on the V2 worker
items.description: Add a worker executor that prompts the model named on the specification with the artifact package and human scores as reference hints, then returns structured JSON (missed requirements, invented requirements, optional alignment score, recommended improvements, confidence) plus a markdown appendix. Validate the JSON against the schema on the specification and mark the job failed when it does not match.
definitionOfDone: Valid output stores structured JSON and a markdown appendix in Blob
Output that fails schema validation marks the job failed
Human scores are passed only as hints
Tests cover valid output, invalid output and model errors
technicalDependencies: Model client used by existing V2 lanes
Judge output schema from the definition
nonFunctionalRequirements: Judge output never overwrites human scores
Worker uses only the model and limits carried on the specification

items.title: Ingest job results on App Service
items.description: Handle completion callbacks or run results on App Service, since the worker has no database. Update each job row's status, summary and Blob references, and expose the judge's recommended improvements and the Promptfoo failure state for the admin views. Completion triggers no notification.
definitionOfDone: Job rows move through pending, running, ready or failed
Repeated completion messages do not duplicate results
Summary and Blob references are available to the admin read operations
Tests cover success, failure and duplicate delivery
nonFunctionalRequirements: Ingest is idempotent for repeated completion messages
Ingest failure leaves the human event unchanged

features.title: Promptfoo and LLM Judge Execution
outOfScope: Using judge output to change human scores
features.description: Gives Project Admin and Platform Admin users structured diagnostics, a Promptfoo result and judge recommendations, by running both checks on the V2 worker and storing the results.
dependencies: V2 worker runtime with no database access

outOfScope: Per-project daily caps on judge runs
assumptions: The judge model is the project evaluation model when set, otherwise the PRD validation default

businessRules.rule: Evaluation events are append-only. No operation updates or deletes an event. Resubmitting creates a new event.

Every submission must score all five criteria (intent alignment, requirements coverage, scope alignment, acceptance criteria, readiness) from 1 to 5 and choose exactly one outcome: accept unchanged, accept after edits, regenerate or reject.

When any criterion is 2 or lower, the submission must include at least one reason code from the stage definition and a comment of at least the minimum length set in the definition. This applies to PRD and Interview phase submissions.
A PRD submission with outcome accept after edits must include a corrected artifact. The server uses a snapshot of the current PRD markdown and accepts pasted text when the PRD was not edited in Apex.
An Interview phase submission never requires a corrected artifact. A corrected phase summary may be pasted, and no full transcript rewrite is asked for.
The server resolves skill path, skill version, model, Interview id and PRD id for every event. The client cannot supply or change them.

Every event stores the content hash of the artifact the reviewer saw: PRD markdown plus canonical backlog JSON for a PRD, or the phase transcript slice plus linked context for an Interview phase. History defaults to events matching the live artifact hash, with a control to show older ones.

Human evaluation is advisory. No missing, low-scoring, regenerate or reject evaluation blocks phase advance, Generate PRD, reviewer approval or owner final approval. Regenerate and reject outcomes do not regenerate a PRD or change PRD status.

The server derives reviewer role from the submitter's project groups. One matching group is pre-filled and read-only. Several groups or none require a pick from the stage definition's role list. Free text is never accepted.
Every human submission creates exactly one Promptfoo job and one LLM judge job, unique per event and evaluator. Reading an event never enqueues a job.
A failed or missing job never changes or removes the human event. Failed jobs are retried only by a manual retry. There is no automatic retry.
Judge output is structured JSON validated against the definition's schema plus a markdown appendix. Human scores reach the judge as reference hints only and never overwrite the stored human event.
An in-app alert goes to Project Admins only when an event has outcome regenerate or reject. Job completion sends no alert and Teams is not used.
The feedback surfaces, the Workflow evaluations page, the hub and all evaluation routes are available only when the workflow-human-evaluation flag is on for the project.
Events are always scoped to one project. Definitions are platform seeds shared by all projects and are not forked per project in v1.

The feedback modal appears at most once for a given subject and stage that has no event. After a skip or submit, only the feedback panel and a dismissible banner remain. Skipping never blocks the workflow.
The judge model is resolved on App Service: the project evaluation model when set, otherwise the PRD automated validation default. The worker uses only values carried on the execution specification.
History lists return newest first and are capped at about 50 events per subject.
The Workflow evaluations page is open to anyone who can open Project Admin for the project, and to Platform Admins. The cross-project hub is open to Platform Admins only.

assumptionsMade: Gating is advisory. The transcript first asked for required rubrics at Interview phase ends and PRD owner sign-off, then asked for optional feedback and no hard block. The final lock is fully advisory, so the earlier requirements about who must submit are treated as who the product nudges.

"Super Admin" wording maps to Platform Admin. Reviewer personas are Product-Owner, BA, Manager and Developer, the groups that receive default view and submit grants. QA can be granted the permissions but is not a default.
The Interview initiator is a BA, Product-Owner or Manager, the groups allowed to start Interviews. The PRD owner is the document owner and is treated as a Product-Owner for persona purposes.
The exact mapping of default grants for the two new permissions to RBAC roles is confirmed during implementation under the RBAC governance rule.
The minimum comment length for low scores lives in the definition. A seed value of 20 characters is assumed and needs confirmation.
Apex already tracks the Interview phase count (1 or 3) and current phase. If it does not, the Interview hook derives them from existing Interview state without adding columns.
No PRD generation counter is assumed. The artifact hash alone binds an event to a PRD version.
The Project Settings evaluation model may not exist yet. v1 uses it only when present and otherwise falls back to the PRD validation default. v1 does not add a new project setting.
Failed-job retry is open to the same people who can open the Workflow evaluations page.
Alerts go to Project Admins only. Platform Admins are included only if Apex already sends them cross-project admin alerts.
Dismissal of the modal and banner is remembered per user in the browser. A new browser may show the modal once more.
The seeded Promptfoo suite references start with a minimal structural check of the artifact against the rubric. Richer suites follow after the first pilot.
Registry keys follow the accepted Measured Improvement Loop ADR, with process key `orchestrated_workflow` and stage keys for the PRD and each Interview phase.
Corrected artifacts and job outputs are stored in Blob following the existing async infrastructure pattern.

implementationPhases.rationale: Every other epic reads or writes evaluation events, so the tables, seeded definitions, permissions, flag and evaluation service must exist first. Reviewer screens, job orchestration and admin views all call the router built here.
Both epics need only the Phase 1 service and router. Reviewer screens write events and the job work reacts to stored events, so neither depends on the other and they can run in parallel.

The outcomes screen, the hub and the alerts show human events together with job results, so they need both the Phase 1 foundation and the Phase 2 diagnostic jobs. Reviewer screens in Phase 2 produce the events that admins will read.
